questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: Totipotency refers to:
options: Capacity to generate genetically identical plants
Capacity to generate a whole plant from any plant cell/explant
Recovery of healthy plants from diseased plants
questions.solution:
The technique of growth of plant cells, tissues, or organs in an artificially prepared nutrient medium under aseptic and controlled conditions of light and temperature is called tissue culture. 
Plant tissue culture was first studied by Gottlieb Haberlandt. The concept of tissue culture is based on the property of the totipotency of the plant cells. The ability or potential of any living plant cell or explant to produce all the differentiated cells in an organism is called totipotency.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: Inbreeding depression is:
options: Reduced motility and immunity due to close inbreeding
Decreased productivity due to mating of superior male and inferior female
Decrease in body mass of progeny due to continued close inbreeding
Reduced fertility and productivity due to continued close inbreeding
questions.solution: Inbreeding refers to the mating of closely related animals within the same breed for about 4-6 generations. Inbreeding helps in the development of animals of genetic purity. It promotes homozygosity and expression of recessive genes is observed. Continuous inbreeding leads to inbreeding depression, which affects the productivity and quality of animal products as well as health. The inbreeding depression can be eliminated by crossing animals to the same breed's superior animal but having no common ancestors on both sides.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement regarding inbreeding.
options: Inbreeding helps in the elimination of deleterious alleles from the population
Inbreeding is necessary to evolve a pureline in any animal
Continued inbreeding reduces fertility and leads to inbreeding depression
Inbreeding depression cannot be overcome by outcrossing
questions.solution:
The incorrect statement regarding inbreeding is the option (d). It is because continuous inbreeding among cattle causes inbreeding depression. It decreases the fertility and even productivity of an animal. It can be overcome by applying outbreeding in which mating is done between different breeds or individuals of the same breed but having no common ancestors.
Outbreeding includes outcrossing, cross-breeding and interspecific hybridisation.

questions.q: In case of a couple where the male is having a very low sperm count, which of the following technique will be suitable for fertilization?
questions.solution:
ARTIFICIAL INSEMINATION (AI): The introduction of seminal fluid directly into the uterus of female by artificial method is called artificial insemination. This technique is used in male who have low sperm count and inability to inseminate the female normally. It is of two types:

a) Artificial insemination- homologous (AIH): In this method the semen is collected from husband and is introduced into the vagina or uterus of the female.
b) Artificial insemination- donor (AID): In this method the semen is collected from donor and is introduced into the vagina or uterus of the female.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: Outbreeding is an important strategy of animal husbandry because it:
options: Is useful in producing purelines of animals
Is useful in overcoming inbreeding depression
Expose harmful recessive genes that are eliminated by selection.
Helps in accumulation of superior genes.
questions.solution:
Outbreeding: It refers to the mating of unrelated animals, it may be between individuals of the same breed but not having common ancestors for 4-6 generations. It helps in overcoming inbreeding depression. It is of two types:

Cross–breeding: Mating of animals belonging to different breeds is called cross-breeding. It involves interbreeding of superior males of a breed with superior females of another breed to produce hybrid animals.

Interspecific hybridization: The crossing of male and female animals of two different but related species is called interspecific hybridization. The progeny may have desirable features of both the parents.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q:
Arrange the following steps of somatic hybridisation in a correct sequence.
A. Digestion of cell walls.
B. Isolation of naked protoplasts.
C. Fusion of protoplasts to get hybrid protoplast.
D. Isolation of single cells from two different varieties of plants.
E. Growing of hybrid protoplast to form a new plant.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Somatic hybridisation involves the fusion of protoplasts of two different plant varieties to produce a hybrid plant.

The correct sequence of steps is as follows:

First, single cells are isolated from two different varieties of plants (Step D).

Next, the cell walls of these isolated cells are digested using enzymes such as cellulase and pectinase (Step A).

This digestion results in the isolation of naked protoplasts, which are cells without cell walls (Step B).

The isolated naked protoplasts from the two different varieties are then fused together, often using chemicals like PEG or electrical stimulation, to get a hybrid protoplast (Step C).

Finally, the hybrid protoplast is cultured and grown to form a new plant (Step E).

Thus, the correct sequence is D, A, B, C, E.

Answer: D, A, B, C, E

questions.solution:
A mutation occurs when a DNA gene is damaged or changed in such a way as to alter the genetic message carried by that gene.

It is possible to induce mutations artificially through the use of chemicals or radiations (like gamma radiations), and selecting and using the plants that have the desired character as a source in breeding – this process is called mutation breeding.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement.
options: Inbreeding is essential to evolve purelines in any animal.
Inbreeding helps in accumulation of superior genes and elimination of undesirable genes.
Inbreeding selects harmful recessive genes that reduce fertility and productivity.
questions.solution:
The breeding strategy based on inbreeding is as follows. Superior cows and the superior bulls of the same breed are identified and mated in pairs. The progeny obtained from such mating is evaluated and superior males and females are identified for further mating. A superior female, in the case of cattle, is the cow that produces more milk or lactation. On the other hand, a superior male is that bull, which gives rise to superior progeny as compared to those of other males. Inbreeding, as a rule, increases homozygosity.

  • Advantage: Inbreeding exposes harmful recessive genes that are eliminated by selection. It also helps in the accumulation of superior genes and elimination of less desirable genes. Therefore, this approach increases the productivity of inbred population.
  • Disadvantage: But continued inbreeding, especially close inbreeding, usually reduces fertility and even productivity (inbreeding depression). Whenever this becomes a problem the selected animals of the breeding population should be mated with such superior animals of the same breed that are unrelated to those in the breeding population.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: In order to obtain virus-free plants through tissue culture the best method is:
questions.solution:
The virus infected plants only the meristematic cells of the apical dome are devoid of virus. Therefore, by using shoot apical meristem culture, virus free plants can be raised.
Related Theory
In the meristem there is no cells differentiation. Virus can't move from cell to cell through plasmodesmesta using their Movement protein.
Meristematic cells are considered as virus free because:
(1) Meristematic cells have high multiplication rate than viral cell multiplication rates.
(2) Viruses generally move in plant body through vascular bundles. There is the absence of vascular bundles in meristematic regions.
(3) High auxin concentration and cytokinin concentration and low pH value at which viruses could not survive.
(4) High metabolic activity.
(5) RNA silencing mechanism. According to some findings, it has been hypothesized that the defense systems in meristematic regions treat viruses as foreign particles thus prevent the viruses into the meristematic regions.

questions.q: What is true for individuals of same species?
questions.solution:
A species is a group of similar organisms that can breed with one another to produce fertile offspring. Individuals of the same species can reproduce to make more individuals of the same species. Two individuals belonging to different species cannot normally reproduce together. Niche represents the habitat and functions of a species. Habitat is a specific place where an organism lives.
Related Theory

questions.q: In cloning of cattle a fertilized egg is taken out of the mother's womb and:
options: in the eight cell stage, cells are separated and cultured until small embryos are formed which are unplanted into the womb of other cows
in the eight cell stage the individual cells are separated under electrical field for further development on culture media
from this upto eight identical twins can be produced
the egg is divided into 4 pair; of cells which arc implanted into the womb of other cows.
questions.solution: In the cloning of cattle, a fertilized egg is taken out of the mother's womb. In the eight-cell stage, cells are separated and cultured until small embryos are formed. Later, these are implanted in the womb of a different cow i.e., the host mother. Related Theory Dolly is the first sheep which was developed by the technique of cloning. The sheep was developed from the diploid body cell. The somatic cell from the mother sheep was taken and the nucleus was injected into the egg cell which was cultured and transferred into the surrogate mother. This method is known as nuclear transfer. The sheep Dolly was identical in the characters with the mother who donated the diploid nucleus from the body cell. (Ref. to Fig. 25.5)

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
questions.q: In maize, hybrid vigour is exploited by:
options: crossing of two inbred parental lines
harvesting seeds from the most productive plants
questions.solution:
The increase in the traits of hybrid strength due to crossing over is called hybrid vigour or heterosis. The hybrid vigour in maize is exploited by crossing of an inbred parental line.
Related Theory
The explanation for heterosis phenomenon is based on ideas: (i) every trait of an organism depends on many genes. (ii) Inbreeding depression and heterosis are related to individual genetic diversity. The changes of individual genetic diversity caused by selfpollination and cross-pollination reveals that self-pollinating plants of natural crosspollinating leads to the decrease in individual genetic diversity of offspring and crossing between pure lines of genetic difference leads to the increase in individual genetic diversity. Thus, the decrease in individual genetic diversity is the cause the of depression and the increase in individual genetic diversity is the cause of heterosis.

questions.q: Fishes in eutrophic lake die due to
questions.solution: Eutrophic lakes have high levels of biological productivity due to the rich nutrient constituents, especially nitrogen and phosphorus. An abundance of plants are supported in this lake. Initially, eutrophic lakes accelerate multiplication and growth of lake fauna. Plants and/ or algal blooms overcrowd the lake, they later die and decomposition of dead organic matter starts which leads to decrease in dissolved oxygen content. Decrease in dissolved oxygen suffocats lake fauna, e.g., fishes to death.

questions.subject: Zoology

questions.q:
Assertion : Protandry and protogyny ensure cross fertilisation in some animals.
Reason: Cross fertilisation introduces variation in progeny.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Most of the sexually reproducing animals are either males or females. But in some lower animals, the organs of both the sexes are found in the same individual. These are called bisexual or monoecious animals or hermaphrodites. In these animals, testes and ovaries do not mature simultaneously. In some, testes mature earlier, while in others, ovaries mature earlier. These conditions are respectively called protandry and protogyny. They ensure cross fertilisation. Cross fertilisation is a process in which gametes derived from different individuals are united to form zygote. It involves the mixing of two different genetic materials. It is better than self-fertilisation as it introduces variation by combining traits of two individuals.

Reason: GM foods have mutated genes which cause infections and allergies.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
Ifboth assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
The GM crops are fast becoming a part of agriculture throughout the world because of their contribution to the increased crop productivity and to global food, feed and fiber security, besides their use in health-care and industry.
However, GM foods are facing widespread resistance by the peoplefrom all over the world. It is because transgenes in commercial crops can endanger native species. For example, the gene for Bt toxin expressed in pollen might endanger pollinators like honeybees. These crops cause problems in human health by supplying allergens and transfer of antibiotic resistance markers. The GM crops may change the fundamental vegetable nature of plants as the genes from animals (e.g., fish or mouse) are being introduced into crop plants. GM foods also have a bad effect on environment and biodiversity.

Reason : A number of symbiotic bacteria are present in rumen of cattle.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
questions.solution: The cattles, buffaloes, goats, sheep, deer and camels are herbivorous animals that feed on plant leaves, twigs, etc. Their stomach consists of 4 chambers: rumen (paunch), reticulum (honeycomb), omasum (psalterium) and abomasum (rennet). In the rumen, food undergoes mechanical and chemical breakdown. Mechanical breakdown results from thorough churning brought about by muscular contractions and aided by cornified surface of villi. Chemical breakdown is caused by symbiotic micro-organisms bacteria such as Ruminococcus and ciliate such as Entodinium caudatum. These micoorganisms live as symbionts in the rumen and reticulum of the stomach of the ruminants (e.g., cows and buffaloes) and in the large intestine of other herbivorous mammals (e.g., horses and donkeys) and release enzymes, cellulases, which act on cellulose and simplify it to shortchain fatty acids. Cellulose is not digested in human being.

questions.q: Assertion : Inbreeding increases homozygosity, thus exposes harmful recessive genes, which are eliminated by selection.Reason : Continued inbreeding reduces fertility and productivity.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
questions.solution: When the offsprings are produced by self fertilization or breeding between closely related parents it is called inbreeding. Inbreeding results in increase in homozygosity. The most revealing impact of inbreeding is the loss of vigour and physiological efficiency of the organisms characterized by reduction in size. A number of lethal and defective characters appear in the population which has undergone inbreeding (selfing). This loss of fitness in the progenies or decline in character expression with decreased heterozygosity arising from self mating is known as inbreeding depression or inbreeding decline. Continued inbreeding reduces fertility and even productivity. But the inbreeding progeny with lethal and harmful recessive genes being homozygous express these traits which otherwise remain hidden in heterozygous individuals. Natural selection works upon these individuals and eliminate them. Gradually, such genes get eliminated from the population.

questions.solution: Inbreeding refers to the mating of closely related individuals within the same breed for 46 generations. Superior males and superior females of the same breed are identified and mated in pairs. The progeny obtained from such matings are evaluated and superior males and females among them are identified for further mating. Inbreeding increases homozygosity. Thus inbreeding is necessary if we want to evolve a pureline in any animal.

options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion

questions.solution:
Superovulation is an effort to increase the fertility of cattle breeds. Inducing an animal to ovulate multiple oocytes can translate into producing more offspring from selected females. For superovulation. donor cows of particularly fine pedigree are treated with hormones (mainly FSH and LH) to increase the number of eggs released at ovulation - multiple ovulation (MO). The cows are artificially inseminated using semen from a proven bull.
After 6 - 7 days the embryos are collected non-surgically, and then implanted into recipient cows whose oestrous cycle is at the correct receptive stage - usually as the result of hormonal manipulation.
